cases.question: Can my company ask the tax service for a written ruling on how a law applies before we go ahead with a deal?

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how a tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amend or replace the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give written reasons for being unable to issue it.
An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more such parties.

An advance ruling is defined to include a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, a proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.

An application must contain the taxpayer's contact details, a complete description of the tax issue or transaction (including financial implications, if any), a description of the impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person, details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions, the legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.
The tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or persons connected to the applicant.
A ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, is rendered on the set of facts before the tax authority, and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction actually carried out is materially different from the one described, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption or condition set by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerns is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation on which it is based.

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4): The National Assembly text requires companies in the priority sector to obtain a certificate of acceptance from the Industrial Inspectorate Department for qualifying capital expenditure; the gazette has no such condition. (DR-039)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)
